note: Animate CSS is a pure asset-library wrapper: it registers one Drupal library (animate_css/animate) whose CSS is animate.css v4 at /libraries/animate.css/animate.css (from the Composer package drupal-shimmy/animate.css 4.1.1) and attaches it on every page via hook_page_attachments(). No config, configure route, permissions, plugins or schema. Easy cases are grounded in the real class contract (animate__animated + animate__<effect>) and the library id/path. Because the module stores no per-site config, the medium introspection cases read stable live site state via the library.discovery service (library id + installed path). Hard cases exercise the real usage contract: create content that carries the correct animate.css v4 class names, verified against the stored node body.

evals.prompt: I have the Drupal animate_css module enabled. How do I actually make an element animate — which CSS classes do I add for, say, a bounce entrance? Give the exact class names for this version of the module.
evals.expected_output: animate_css ships animate.css v4, which uses the double-underscore prefix. Add the base class animate__animated plus an effect class, e.g. class="animate__animated animate__bounce". Utility classes like animate__delay-2s, animate__slow and animate__infinite are also available. The pre-v3 unprefixed names (animated bounce) do not work.

evals.prompt: The animate_css Drupal module says it needs the animate.css library. Which asset library does it attach and where on disk must the animate.css file be placed for the module to work?
evals.expected_output: It defines the asset library animate_css/animate whose CSS is the root-relative path /libraries/animate.css/animate.css, i.e. the file must live at web/libraries/animate.css/animate.css. It is provided by the Composer library package drupal-shimmy/animate.css 4.1.1.

evals.prompt: Does animate_css have a configuration page, and how does the animate.css stylesheet end up on my pages after I enable the module?
evals.expected_output: There is no configuration page (configure is null) and no settings. The module's hook_page_attachments() unconditionally adds the animate_css/animate library to every page render, so the animate.css classes are globally available with no further setup.

evals.prompt: On this running Drupal site, animate_css is enabled. By inspecting the live site (not documentation), name the asset library id that this module attaches on every page.
evals.expected_output: The library id is animate_css/animate (defined in animate_css.libraries.yml as the 'animate' library of the animate_css extension). It is attached in hook_page_attachments().

evals.prompt: On this live Drupal site, determine whether the animate.css library that animate_css depends on is actually installed, and report the filesystem path (relative to the Drupal root) of the CSS file it loads.
evals.expected_output: Using the library.discovery service, animate_css/animate loads libraries/animate.css/animate.css; checking file_exists(DRUPAL_ROOT . '/' . that path) shows it is installed on this site.

evals.prompt: On my Drupal site (which has the animate_css module) I want a new blog-style Article titled 'animate_css_fade demo' whose intro paragraph fades up into view when the page loads. Please create it so the fade-up animation from the animate library will actually run.
evals.expected_output: Create an Article node titled like 'animate_css_fade demo' whose body wraps the intro text in an element with class="animate__animated animate__fadeInUp". The verify checks the stored body contains both animate__animated and animate__fadeInUp.
